results.title: How Students Use—and Hide—AI in Online Assessments and ...
results.content: This targeted survey focused on students’ experiences with online assessments, use of AI tools, and related ethical concerns. To understand how students view the evolving role of AI tools in academic work, we asked them to respond to three broad policy statements in **Q8: AI Acceptable**: (1) AI is acceptable if used for support but not to generate full answers, (2) AI should not be allowed at all in graded assessments, and (3) AI use should be encouraged provided citation guidance is given. These findings, when viewed alongside the broader patterns of disclosure behaviour and ethical concerns explored earlier, point to important tensions and opportunities in how institutions might foster transparency, trust in student work, and constructive AI use through both policy and assessment design, a theme we now examine in the Discussion. This paper reports on a small-scale survey of undergraduate economics students, exploring their perceptions, behaviours, and ethical concerns around the use of AI tools in online assessments.

results.content: * What it enables: AI transforms education through personalized learning, automated grading, and adaptive assessments tailored to individual student needs. You can train **Disco AI, our native AI tool**; not an extension of ChatGPT, to personalize the learning journeys of your students. By integrating game-like elements into the learning journey, AI not only engages students but also motivates them to excel in ways that traditional assessments cannot. Interactive AI bots are transforming the educational landscape by actively engaging students in their learning journey. These AI-powered tools offer dynamic support that complements the role of human educators, ensuring that the collaborative learning experience is both enriched and effective. By incorporating AI-generated prompts into group work activities, educators can create a more dynamic and interactive learning environment that promotes active engagement and deep learning, helping to motivate students. Open dialogue between educators and students regarding the integration of AI into the learning process is essential to ensure that assessments remain credible and fair.
